subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chat isolation be solved by automatic per-sender subagents, by account/sender-scoped group sessions plus explicit bindings, or by a narrower context-policy fix?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested shape dynamically creates agents/config/workspaces from group senders and changes memory, skills, permissions, session lifecycle, and operating cost in shared Feishu groups.

options.title: Use scoped sessions and bindings first
options.body: Keep group isolation in Feishu session routing and explicit bindings, add only missing plugin API/config pieces, and avoid default dynamic subagent trees.

options.title: Adopt group dynamic subagents
options.body: Design explicit lifecycle, quotas, admin commands, memory/skill boundaries, and live Feishu proof before implementing automatic per-sender agents.

options.title: Defer to narrower issues
options.body: Resolve multi-bot account/session collision and context-pollution issues before revisiting full per-user group subagents.

recommendation.title: Use scoped sessions and bindings first
recommendation.body: Keep group isolation in Feishu session routing and explicit bindings, add only missing plugin API/config pieces, and avoid default dynamic subagent trees.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu package declares @m1heng as the community-maintained plugin owner signal, making them the best available decision owner for channel-specific product behavior.
